This prevents empty or redundant prompt sections from being included.

eli5.text: When you're using an AI agent, the system builds a prompt for itself by gathering instructions and tool descriptions. Previously, even when no tools were actually available to the agent, the system could still include empty or redundant sections meant to list those tools and instructions, cluttering the prompt. Now, those tool-listing sections come back completely blank instead when there are no tools, so the built prompt stays clean and avoids unnecessary content. This makes the prompt that gets sent to the AI neater behind the scenes, without affecting how you interact with the agent.

eli5.text: The internal tools that test AI assistants on our code (an automated judge, a trace analyzer, and a task generator) had their official names cleaned up by removing the old 'git-evals2' prefix, so they are now simply called the AI judge, the trace analyzer, and the task generator. These are only used by our internal team to grade how well our AI helpers perform, so regular writers won't see anything different. A small part of the testing toolkit also got safer: if one of its setup steps runs into an error now, it will quietly report the problem in the logs instead of crashing a whole test run. The change is live for our internal testers today, but it does not change anything that shows up in your document or on your screen.

ai.title: Refine base2 agent completion prompts
ai.summary: Updated base2.ts prompts to allow short bullet points for task completion summaries and added explicit 'keep working' instruction for max mode. The step prompt now conditionally enforces completion before summarizing.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task it was asked to do, it can now report what changed using a short sentence or a few bullet points instead of writing a full paragraph. This applies to people who trigger the high-power planning mode, where the assistant is also told to keep working until they are truly done instead of stopping at the first reasonable answer. The change is live today.

ai.title: Fix codesearch formatting bug
ai.summary: Ripgrep output parser now handles filenames containing hyphens or colons by using regex patterns for match and context lines instead of naive `indexOf(':')`. Separator lines (`--`) are explicitly skipped. Applied to `common/src/util/format-code-search.ts`, `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`, and `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts`.

eli5.text: You asked the assistant's code-search tool to look for text inside files, and it used to mix up the file name when that name contained a hyphen or a colon. Now the results are sorted correctly again. The fix also tells the tool where to find lines that are just context around each match, so nothing appears out of place. The corrected behavior is live today.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search through code, the results now always show which line number each match is on. Previously, line numbers could be missing from the search results, which sometimes made it hard to read the output correctly; the search now consistently includes them. This applies to both the developer kit (the tools other builders use to connect to the assistant) and the desktop app, so anyone relying on those code-search features will notice line numbers are always present now. The change is live today.

ai.summary: CLI authentication logic refactored to use @tanstack/react-query, replacing manual state management in chat.tsx and index.tsx with useAuthQuery and useLoginMutation hooks. This change introduces dependency injection for testability and standardizes error handling via QueryClient. The update affects cli/src/hooks/use-auth-query.ts, cli/src/chat.tsx, and cli/src/index.tsx, requiring @tanstack/react-query as a new dependency.

eli5.text: The command line tool now remembers you're logged in instead of asking every time, so signing in works smoothly without repeated login prompts. Behind the scenes, the program swapped out its homemade login tracking for a standard system that manages your session more reliably. If you use the tool today, logging in and staying logged in should feel steadier, and the developers added new tests to catch login problems before they reach you.

ai.title: CLI login typecheck
ai.summary: Added explicit `ValidatedUserInfo` type and return annotation to `validateApiKey` in `use-auth-query.ts`. Updated `pollLoginStatus` in `login-flow.ts` to safely cast `data.user` via intermediate `rawUser` check. Fixes TypeScript errors in CLI login flow. Affects `cli/src/hooks/use-auth-query.ts` and `cli/src/login/login-flow.ts`.

eli5.text: When you sign in to the tool on the command line, the program now checks the returned account details more carefully before trusting them, so a sign-in that previously failed type-checking can now complete. The login polling step now verifies the account object is actually present and shaped correctly before using it, and the validation function now declares exactly what account fields it expects to return. This is a behind-the-scenes fix to stop login errors, and it is live today.

ai.title: Consolidate terminal breakpoints into reusable hook
ai.summary: New `useTerminalBreakpoints` hook centralizes responsive logic previously inline in `login-modal.tsx`. It derives width/height flags (`isNarrow`, `isVerySmall`, etc.) from `@opentui/react` renderer dimensions. `LoginModal` now consumes this hook, removing direct `useRenderer` calls and manual breakpoint calculations. Includes `isTall` alias for backward compatibility.

eli5.text: When you open the CLI login screen, the layout now adapts smoothly to different terminal sizes using a single shared rule set. Instead of each part of the login screen calculating on its own how wide or tall the terminal is, they all ask the same centralized helper for breakpoint flags like isNarrow or isVerySmall. You might notice the login modal renders correctly no matter how small or large you resize your terminal window. The helper uses fixed thresholds: width below 60 columns is narrow, 60 - 99 is medium width, 100+ is wide; height below 15 rows is very small, 15 - 19 is small, 20 - 29 is medium, 30+ is large. This is live today for anyone running the CLI login flow. The new helper replaces direct inline calls, and the login screen now reads from it directly rather than duplicating the

The CLI (`npm-app`) renders these updates as a checkbox list, suppressing intermediate chunks for cleaner output. This change spans core tool definitions, handlers, and type mappings across multiple packages.

eli5.text: When you give the AI assistant a task with multiple steps, it can now keep a running checklist that shows up in your conversation. Instead of just talking through what it's doing, the assistant writes down each step and marks them off as it finishes, so you see a clear list of completed and pending items. The CLI interface renders these updates as a checkbox list, suppressing intermediate chunks for cleaner output. This is live today for anyone using the agent runtime to run multi-step tasks.

ai.title: SDK 0.5.2 bundles agent runtime, env, and codesearch improvements
ai.summary: This release bump packages the same-day 0.5.x work: SDK agent lifecycle now POSTs agent steps with apiKey and returns stepId (post-0.22), run-terminal-command gains a SIGKILL fallback after SIGTERM timeout, and the local agent runtime is wired behind getAgentRuntimeImpl with consumeCreditsWithFallback and injected fetch/logger deps. Environment plumbing was extended so CodebuffClient and run() accept a merging env parameter, NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars are inlined into the build, and dev/test gating activates skipValidation. Agent-side behavior changed with base2 gaining a decomposing-thinker option, task-researcher2 and planner-pro-with-files-input, base2-fast-todos using write_todos, and codesearch adding -n line numbers plus per-file (15) and global (250) result caps with hyphen/colon-safe parsing. Prompt caching and message tagging were hardened, the web /me handler moved to an App Router route, and CLI auth switched to TanStack Query with a deferred (non-blocking) login modal.
ai.evidence: sdk/package.json hunk changes version from 0.5.1 to 0.5.2 only (+1/-1); earlier same-day 2025-10-27 commits (0469a3f7 generateText cost metadata, 2bc86071 addAgentStep injection, 22/Oct SDK lifecycle + billing stubs, 23/Oct base2 variant + runId tracing, 24/Oct env threading, 25/Oct codesearch limits, 26/Oct tags-based prompt cache, 27/Oct terminal breakpoint hook and SDK build/LLM import refactors) are the user-visible work folded into this release

eli5.text: This release upgrades the Freebuff CLI to version 0.5.2, bringing faster agent modes, improved login security, and clearer code search results along with a new way for developers to track and manage their AI coding tasks. A major highlight is the shift to browser-based login: instead of waiting on complicated auth setups, you now get a simple screen that opens in your browser where you can log in once and keep working without extra steps. Code search (when you ask the AI to find something across your project) is now grouped by file and reports line numbers correctly, even for tricky filenames, so you get cleaner and more reliable results. The CLI now shows your loaded agents in a collapsible panel at startup, and you can toggle between fast and max agent modes on the fly using a new Shift+Tab shortcut, giving you quick control over how thorough you want each request to be. Power users and developers get extra goodies too: new task-tracking tools for the AI, cost-tracking on responses, and a cleaner SDK so custom extensions built on Freebuff stay consistent. Upgrading gives users smoother authentication, a more responsive and informative CLI interface, and more accurate search and task-planning capabilities without any breaking changes to existing workflows.

Uses `bun scripts/generate-ci-env.js` to determine variable names, then extracts corresponding values from `SECRETS_CONTEXT` via `jq`. Explicitly sets `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Version in `sdk/package.json` reverted from `0.5.3` to `0.5.1`.

eli5.text: When the system builds and releases the software kit for programmers, it now automatically gathers the necessary passwords and settings and hands them to the release process, so the build can access the right accounts and turn on the special automation mode. To a person downloading or updating the kit, this change is invisible, although they may notice that the kit's reported version number has been dialed back from 0.5.3 to 0.5.1, as if the most recent release was being re-issued rather than advanced forward.

This release includes a CI fix where the sdk-release-build workflow now injects environment variables (CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS, CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN) via generate-ci-env.js and jq extraction from SECRETS_CONTEXT. The release also reverts an unintended version bump back to 0.5.1 before applying the correct 0.5.2 increment. No functional code changes shipped with this version bump.

eli5.text: The Freebuff SDK has been updated to version 0.5.2, which improves how the software development kit is built and released through GitHub's automated systems. Upgrading gives you a smoother, more dependable experience when using or building on top of the Freebuff SDK.

Developers using the SDK will benefit from more stable and reliable interactions with the underlying AI coding assistant, ensuring smoother integration into their projects. ai.title: directory-lister switch to structured output
ai.summary: directory-lister agent in .agents/file-explorer/directory-lister.ts changes outputMode from 'all_messages' to 'structured_output'. handleSteps now accumulates list_directory JSON results into a toolResults array, then yields set_output with the combined array. toolNames updated to include 'set_output'. Import JSONObject and JSONValue from types/util-types.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that lists file directories now provides its findings in a cleaner, more organized format. Instead of returning a long stream of raw text messages, it collects all the directory contents into a single structured package and labels each item with the path it came from. This makes the output easier to read and use for anything that processes the results automatically. The change only affects internal tooling used by developers.
